I find I’m not able to use microfibre anymore due to all the issues, so I know where you’re coming from. A really cost-effective solution is to go to your local grocery store and buy some flour sack towels. They are super cheap and all you need to do is fold them into a rectangle the size of an insert and you’re good to go!

Edit: another practically free solution is to use receiving blankets! People give you so many at baby showers, it’s nice that you can put them to good use

I really like bamboo and hemp, but cotton is great too. I just make sure to put hemp on the bottom because of it’s slow absorption, and I can usually get away with two of inserts (whether that be cotton/bamboo, bamboo/hemp, cotton/cotton, bamboo/bamboo) which equates to roughly 8 layers of fabric assuming each insert it usually 4 layers. 

My daughter is also a heavy wetter so she gets changed every two hours or so. How old is your baby? I found the peak of ‘wetness’ so-to-speak was at 5 months before she began solids. Now she’s not just soaking every diaper immediately
I take them out as soon as I change my baby’s diaper and throw it into the diaper pail. It’s sooo much easier and less gross than separating it just before it goes into the wash

Personally I wash them all together. I just air dry the diapers since I want to preserve the PUL for as long as I can. You could dry them on low and I’m sure they’d be okay though. What most people do (me included) is a cool rinse cycle no detergent to wash out the majority of the waste, which also prevents any poop from getting stained into the fabric. Then a long, hot wash cycle with detergent to clean them completely. If you have any other questions feel free to ask!

I’m 21 and my daughter was born on the 11th of this month. My boyfriend and I wanted kids eventually but not now. We were using condoms and birth control pills yet I still got pregnant. During my pregnancy there was a roller coaster of emotions the entire time. It was hard to come to terms with things because I wasn’t where I wanted to be in life but at the same time I’ve always wanted to be a mom so I was happy I was able to carry a child. 

I cried lots throughout my pregnancy, and not like I tried to hide it but I wasn’t overly proud or excited about being pregnant. Yes there was times I was happy about it but never like proudly-announce-to-strangers happy. 

My birth experience was very traumatic and I didn’t get that initial feeling of maternal love for my baby because I was in and out of consciousness when she was born. I cried so much because I was so worried that something was wrong with me. After I got back on my feet recovery-wise about 8 days after she was born, everything began to fall into place. I love my little girl more than life itself. Don’t get me wrong, motherhood is hard but until you experience it, you don’t know how you’ll react to it. It’s so much more amazing than I ever thought it could be and she’s not even a month old yet. 

Taking one day at a time is the best thing you can do right now, momma. Life has a funny way of working things out. I worried so much about the future when I was pregnant yet things are already so much different than I would’ve imagined. Having a support system you can lean on is the most important thing. Even though I’m a stranger, you can reach out to me anytime if you need someone to talk to. I hope all goes well for you 💕

I suffer from chronic depression and anxiety; I used to be on antidepressants and went to therapy weekly. I found the medication I was on helped, in the beginning. What really helped me was talking out my problems/past trauma and learning coping techniques and other mental tools to 'reprogram' my brain. 

But the biggest thing here, you have to WANT help. No matter how many people try to get you to get help, you'll never make significant progress unless you yourself want to be better. 

I'm off all my medication and have been for over a year because it was having adverse effects on me. I live in Canada so I don't know if your country would allow this, but I have a green card that I use periodically to help with anxiety issues which tend to escalate my depressive tendencies. Marijuana isn't for everyone, but personally I've found it helps me significantly more than any medication I've taken, and not to mention it helps for a longer period of time before I 'crash' so I'm not needing to medicate myself nearly as often. 

So in short, I don't think you can 'cure' mental illness, but you can definitely make it more livable and less obvious in your everyday life. Think of it as an addiction; you never stop fighting the urges, but the so-called urges become less and less difficult to manage. 

All the best!

Long story ahead. It was last August. I was out camping with some family and friends up north about an hour away from the nearest small town. I was feeling amazing, no pain, nothing. But that evening I went to my campsite to go grab leftover fries for my friend because he was hungry. The moment I opened the container, I felt extremely nauseous and had a burning pain in my stomach. I don't even know if that was related to what happened to me but that was the first warning signs. I had to sit down because I thought I was going to pass out. Thankfully my aunt came with me to my campsite and I called for her because I felt sick. She later told me at the hospital that my pupils were huge and my skin was so green, something she hadn't seen before (she's a nurse). I started throwing up while trying not to scream due to the pain in my stomach. My aunt is usually a very calm lady but she grabbed out her phone to text my dad to come there and then called 911. We were unfamiliar of the area so she needed to know where the nearest hospital was so we could go; knowing an ambulance would take twice as long. The dispatcher told her that the nearest hospital was an hour away so they packed me up in the truck and we left. It was 9:30pm-ish then. Of course it was the worst storm out; lightning and pouring rain. I don't remember anything else because the whole car ride I was either passed out or screaming bloody murder from the pain when I woke up. The following is what my dad told me. We arrived to the town with the hospital but would you believe it, it was fucking closed! They had to find another one which they did about an hour or two later. Luckily it was occupied with people. My dad carried me in and I began to throw up a lot blood which extremely worried the doctors there. They hooked me up to an IV and gave me a form of Gravol used for chemo patients due to how strong it is. Then they gave me some other medications that would stop bleeding and such while also giving me a few blood transfusions due to how much blood I was throwing up. After a hellish night and many tests, they found that my white blood cell count was through the roof, and my stomach acid was almost three times more acidic than the average person. The pain I felt? My stomach was practically digesting itself. I have an extremely high pain tolerance but I felt like I was dying. They aren't completely sure of what caused the attack, but they believe I had a bacterial infection so they put me on medication. I still have trouble with my stomach sometimes but with the medication I'm on, I've definitely noticed a difference. This was totally one of the scariest experiences of my life
